html:
CRYPTO NEWS — July 27, 2026

As the US and Iran pause missile strikes, Bitcoin holds firm above $65,000 while Ethereum leads the upside—but don't confuse modest gains with conviction. The Fear & Greed Index barely budged to 30 from yesterday's 26, and participants are positioning carefully for the July 28–29 FOMC meeting. This is consolidation masquerading as strength. Ethereum's 4.20% 24h pop signals capital rotation into alts, but breadth is thin. Bitcoin has recovered from July's early lows but struggled to sustain breakouts, and traders are in wait-and-see mode ahead of the Fed. Low funding rates across all three majors mean leverage isn't stretched—safety in a sea of macro unknowns.

TODAY'S HIGHLIGHTS

Forma Chain to Shut Down: NFTs Migrating to Ethereum
Forma announced it will gradually shut down its blockchain, with NFTs migrating to Ethereum while users are advised to withdraw assets through the Forma Bridge. This is chain-specific noise—Forma never commanded significant liquidity or developer momentum. The takeaway for traders: small-cap L1s that can't retain ecosystem gravity have nowhere to hide. Don't hold Layer 1 tokens expecting network lock-in if the dev community isn't there.

Storj Labs Files Chapter 11: Decentralized Storage Giant Restructures Legacy Debt
Storj Labs voluntarily filed Chapter 11 on July 26 to address legacy obligations while preserving ongoing operations. STORJ token dropped 14% overnight to $0.06334 by midday July 27 after initially holding near $0.074. The critical detail: token holders sit at the bottom of the creditor hierarchy, while the token itself serves genuine utility for storage and bandwidth transactions. This matters for traders—bankruptcy introduces restructuring risk and exchange listing uncertainty for token-dependent businesses. Avoid illiquid altcoins tied to companies with legacy debt loads.

FOMC Decision Wednesday Sets Tone for Week Ahead
The July 28–29 FOMC meeting will test how crypto markets react to Fed Chair Warsh's stance, with interest-rate futures pricing debate about size rather than direction—a quarter-point increase is live and tradable. For crypto investors, reduced Fed guidance signals higher volatility ahead, with Bitcoin's next major move likely tied to incoming inflation data. The trade: set stops tighter ahead of Wednesday's 2 p.m. ET decision. Dollar strength and Fed hawkishness remain the biggest headwinds—Bitcoin pays no yield, making rising rates a direct opportunity cost.

WATCH LIST

24-48 hours: The FOMC decision dominates everything. Bitcoin needs conviction above $65,618 to retest $66,500; a miss and the $64,371 low is in play. Ethereum's 4% pop has room if BTC follows, but alt momentum only holds with sustained broad-market bid. Low funding across the board means no leverage cascade to catch you on the downside—a double-edged sword. DeFi tokens (Aave, Ondo, Compound) showing life; watch for drawdown on Fed hawkishness. Forma and Storj are Chapter 11 shadows—stay away from small-cap ecosystem tokens with restructuring risk.

See you tomorrow — stay sharp and watch the Fed closely.
